420-D04-AB — Conformity Assessment · Cohort CYB-01 · Fall 2026

Lab 0 — Install & verify the auditing tools

Step-by-step visual walkthrough · nine steps · everything shown is current as of October 2026, with a footnote under each step for newer versions

Before you start

Tools run only on your two lab VMs (virtual machines) under the written course mandate — never on college, employer, home or third-party systems (Canada Criminal Code s. 342.1). Take the clean snapshots first. Mask real personal information in every screenshot. Full requirements: Legal notice.

Step 1 — Take a “clean” snapshot of both VMsStep 2 — Ubuntu VM — install Lynis and Nmap, verify the versionsStep 3 — Ubuntu VM — first Lynis run and the hardening indexStep 4 — Windows VM — CIS-CAT Lite: download, unzip, detect the benchmarkStep 5 — Windows VM — Security Compliance Toolkit and Policy AnalyzerStep 6 — Windows VM — PowerShell checksStep 7 — Both VMs — run the two verification scriptsStep 8 — Merge the results into the Environment checklistStep 9 — Submit through Omnivox LÉA (DropBox)
1

Take a “clean” snapshot of both VMs

Lab 0 · step 1 of 9

Open VirtualBox (or VMware Workstation / the CyberQuébec console), select the VM, open the Snapshots view, click Take, name it clean, add the description “Day 1 – nothing installed yet”, click OK. Repeat on the second VM. Screenshot both snapshot lists.

⬇ Download this animation (GIF)

Evidence and notes

  • Evidence: L0-E01_snapshot-win.png, L0-E02_snapshot-ubuntu.png
  • Why: a snapshot restores the VM in seconds if a tool or a test leaves it in an unknown state.

Footnote — if what you see looks different (versions, October 2026)

VirtualBox 7.2.22 (October 2026): the Snapshots view is reached from the VM’s menu button (the three-line icon next to the VM name) → Snapshots. In VMware Workstation Pro 26H1 (free) the menu is VM → Snapshot → Take Snapshot. On the CyberQuébec range, snapshots are taken from the VM’s console page. A newer VirtualBox or Workstation release may move the button; the name “clean” does not change.

2

Ubuntu VM — install Lynis and Nmap, verify the versions

Lab 0 · step 2 of 9

Open a terminal (Ctrl+Alt+T) and run sudo apt update && sudo apt install -y lynis nmap. Then lynis --version and nmap --version: the version strings are your evidence.

⬇ Download this animation (GIF)

Evidence and notes

  • Evidence: L0-E11_lynis-version.png, L0-E12_nmap-version.png
  • The apt package of Lynis may be older than the GitHub release; either is acceptable for this course — record what you have.

Footnote — if what you see looks different (versions, October 2026)

Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS is the course reference (apt gives Lynis 3.0.9 and Nmap 7.94). If your VM runs Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS — the default download since April 2026 — the commands are identical and apt gives Lynis 3.1.6 and Nmap 7.98. To get the current Lynis 3.1.7 on any release: git clone https://github.com/CISOfy/lynis then cd lynis && sudo ./lynis audit system, or add the CISOfy apt repository (see the Lab 0 guide).

3

Ubuntu VM — first Lynis run and the hardening index

Lab 0 · step 3 of 9

Run sudo lynis audit system. It takes one to three minutes and modifies nothing. At the end, write down the hardening index (a number out of 100) in the checklist. Copy the report with sudo cp /var/log/lynis-report.dat ~/lab0/L0-E14_lynis-report.dat.

⬇ Download this animation (GIF)

Evidence and notes

  • Evidence: L0-E13_lynis-index.png (the end of the output) and the copied report
  • No analysis tonight: the warnings and suggestions become Lab 4 findings on Day 7.

Footnote — if what you see looks different (versions, October 2026)

The same animation is used for steps 2 and 3 (second half). Lynis 3.0.9 and 3.1.7 both print the index as “Hardening index : NN”; 3.0.9 adds a warning that the release is old — ignore it tonight. If a newer major version changes the layout, the index is still in the last block of the output.

4

Windows VM — CIS-CAT Lite: download, unzip, detect the benchmark

Lab 0 · step 4 of 9

Register on the CIS site (free), download the CIS-CAT Lite zip, unzip it into C:\Tools\ (never run it from inside the zip). Start the Assessor (Assessor-GUI.bat or Assessor-CLI.bat from an Administrator prompt), confirm that the Windows 11 (or 10) Enterprise benchmark is listed, pick Level 1, run once with the HTML report option, and save the report.

⬇ Download this animation (GIF)

Evidence and notes

  • Evidence: L0-E23_ciscat.png (benchmark detected) and L0-E25_ciscat_report.html
  • The score tonight is just a number; Lab 4 analyzes the failed recommendations.

Footnote — if what you see looks different (versions, October 2026)

CIS-CAT Lite is CIS-CAT Pro Assessor v4.67.0 (October 5, 2026) running without a licence; since v4.63 it requires Java 21, which the Windows download bundles. Lite covers the Windows 10 Enterprise (v5.0.0), Windows 11 Enterprise (v5.1.0), Google Chrome and Ubuntu 20.04 benchmarks only. If autodetection fails on Windows 11, pick the Windows 11 Enterprise benchmark manually. The registration form, the folder name (Assessor-CLI) and the launcher names can change — look for any file named Assessor-*.bat. The screens in the animation are simplified.

5

Windows VM — Security Compliance Toolkit and Policy Analyzer

Lab 0 · step 5 of 9

Download the Microsoft Security Compliance Toolkit 1.0 from the Microsoft Download Center (select Policy Analyzer and the Windows 11 security baseline zip). Unzip both into C:\Tools\SCT\. Start PolicyAnalyzer.exe, Add… the baseline GPOs as a policy rule set, then Compare to Local Policy. Note three differences.

⬇ Download this animation (GIF)

Evidence and notes

  • Evidence: L0-E24_policyanalyzer.png with the differences visible
  • Policy Analyzer is portable: no installer, just the unzipped folder.

Footnote — if what you see looks different (versions, October 2026)

The toolkit page was updated on October 8, 2026 and lists the Windows 11 version 26H2 Security Baseline v2 next to the 25H2, 24H2 and 23H2 baselines — take the one matching the version shown by winver on your VM. Policy Analyzer 4.0.x looks the same across baseline versions.

6

Windows VM — PowerShell checks

Lab 0 · step 6 of 9

Open PowerShell as Administrator and run Get-ComputerInfo | Select-Object OsName, OsVersion, OsBuildNumber then Get-HotFix | Select-Object -First 5. The first command is slow the first time (10–30 seconds) — this is normal.

⬇ Download this animation (GIF)

Evidence and notes

  • Evidence: L0-E20_computerinfo.png, L0-E22_hotfix.png
  • These two cmdlets are the first checks of Lab 4 (patch verification).

Footnote — if what you see looks different (versions, October 2026)

Windows PowerShell 5.1 is built into Windows 11; PowerShell 7.6 (pwsh, optional, winget install --id Microsoft.PowerShell) gives identical output for these commands. The Windows 11 Enterprise evaluation is version 26H2 (or LTSC 2024, build 26100); the Windows 10 Enterprise evaluation was withdrawn after October 14, 2025, so a Windows 10 VM only exists if you already had one.

7

Both VMs — run the two verification scripts

Lab 0 · step 7 of 9

Copy verify_tools.sh to the Ubuntu VM (chmod +x verify_tools.sh && ./verify_tools.sh) and Verify-Tools.ps1 to the Windows VM (Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope Process Bypass then .\Verify-Tools.ps1). Each writes its half of the checklist as CSV. A MISSING row is a finding, not a failure: fix the cause (usually an unzipped archive) and re-run.

⬇ Download this animation (GIF)

Evidence and notes

  • Output: ~/lab0/environment_checklist_linux.csv and ~\lab0\environment_checklist_windows.csv
  • The scripts are in the Day 1 downloadables (scripts folder).

Footnote — if what you see looks different (versions, October 2026)

Execution-policy syntax is unchanged since PowerShell 5.1. If the Ubuntu VM has no bash in the PATH check (it always has), the script reports MISSING for Bash — which would itself be worth a screenshot.

8

Merge the results into the Environment checklist

Lab 0 · step 8 of 9

Open environment_checklist_template.csv (or the XLSX from the Day 1 downloadables), paste the rows from both CSV files, add the two snapshot rows and the Lynis hardening index, and export the half-page as PDF named LastName_FirstName_420-D04-AB_Lab0_Environment-Checklist.pdf. Keep the screenshots in a folder named lab0-evidence with the names used in the evidence column.

⬇ Download this animation (GIF)

Evidence and notes

  • Deliverable: the PDF + the evidence folder (zipped) — this becomes Chapter 0 of the Course Procedure Manual
  • Mask any real personal information in screenshots (user names, real IP addresses).

Footnote — if what you see looks different (versions, October 2026)

LibreOffice Calc, Excel and Google Sheets all open the CSV files; the column order must stay tool · version · VM · status · evidence.
